title: Short-Corner Baseline Jumpers
description: Players shoot from the short corner along the baseline, a spot reached by baseline drives and zone gaps, using the right footwork off a pass from the wing.

content.objective: Catch and shoot from the short corner with feet set and the shoulders square, without using the backboard.
content.setup: Passer at the wing; shooter in the short corner (between the block and the corner).
instructions: The shooter flashes from the block to the short corner.
Catch the wing pass with feet set behind the ball.
Turn the shoulders to the rim (the angle is sharp: face the rim, not the board).
Shoot with a high arc to clear the rim's near edge.
coachingPoints: Square to the rim: the sharp angle makes this hard.
High arc to drop over the front rim.
Stay a step inside the baseline.
commonMistakes: Shooting while facing the backboard and banking by accident.
Feet on the baseline (out of bounds).
Flat shots that hit the back of the rim.
content.safety: Shooters rebound their own ball only when the lane is clear; nobody stands under the rim while others shoot.
progressions: Shot fake and one dribble to the block.
variations: Short-corner shot off a baseline drive pass.
Use the bank from slightly higher up.
successCriteria: Six makes from each side in two minutes.
content.gameApplication: The short corner is one of the most open spots against zone defenses.
